ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure, an R group is connected to a carbon-carbon triple bond, and the carbon at the right end of the triple bond is connected to Br, which can be read as R-C≡C-Br; at the lower right there is a separate Bu label with a negative sign next to it. The curved arrows in the figure are ignored according to the problem. Reasoning: Represent the unspecified R substituent with the SMILES wildcard *, and write the left alkynyl bromide fragment as *C#CBr. Interpret Bu^- as an ordinary n-butyl anion, with the negative charge on the methylene carbon at the connection end, written as [CH2-]CCC. The two fragments are not connected in the static structure, so separate them with a dot, giving *C#CBr.[CH2-]CCC.

method.method_draft: First visually parse only the static structure: the left fragment is R-C≡C-Br, and there is a separate Bu group bearing a negative charge. Replace the unspecified R substituent by the SMILES wildcard '*', giving the alkynyl bromide fragment '*C#CBr'. Interpret Bu^- as a normal butyl anion with the charged terminal carbon at the attachment point, '[CH2-]CCC'. Since the fragments are not connected in the drawing, join their SMILES with a dot to obtain '*C#CBr.[CH2-]CCC'.
